text:
Bravo, Bai Velichkov! See, I like you this way. Why should we deceive the younger generation? Let’s lay our cards on the table. Ideals! Hogwash! Our own personal earthly contentment—that is the ideal we should pursue. I am glad you have finally reached this truth. And does this vile common folk deserve us killing ourselves for them! While we were younger, it was one thing; but now—we’ve become men of forty years, it’s time to think of ourselves. Enough of this scraping by! Especially you, poor soul, you really suffered through those Istanbul alleys, those Italian ones... wasn't that a whole feat? When you saw Stambolov going on a rampage, you just up and cleared out of Bulgaria, left those slaves behind—let them wallow in their slavery. They’re used to it. You aren’t used to suffering, and like any gentleman, you made sure to bolt. What didn't you endure in that godforsaken Halki—sometimes you didn't even have enough money for medicine. Bobchev and Madzharov kept their mouths shut. Enough with the heroics. And you know what—why don't you just drop your godforsaken poetry too. It’s all well and good, but only when the wind isn't whistling through your purse; but now, thank God, we’ve settled in. 

Now all sorts of brats, little socialists, little idealists, they’ll start yapping at you, but don't you even blink! Turn a deaf ear and just enjoy yourself; and while you're enjoying yourself, laugh at their lack of sense. It’s obvious. Why will they yap at you? Is it for some betrayal of yours, for some deception, out of disappointment? No! Out of envy? Of course! Without a doubt! Without a doubt, out of envy! And why? Simply because their bones were crushed, their throats were torn raw, while you (you’re a clever devil, damn you!) just plopped yourself down into the warmest spot, all ready-made. Well, do you see now? Have you come around? Didn't I tell you that in this world, the best thing is to be warm and cozy? This social struggle, ideals, and I don't know what other nonsense—it's all hogwash! Now, when you hold out your little bag at the end of the month and they shovel fifteen hundred big levs into it... A fine thing, damn it! Hold on tight now! Once you’ve grabbed the bone—hold on! Don't you give a thought to whose skin those levs are being flayed from... Beat the flour sack, damn it all! Beat it! It keeps giving...

But you might wonder why I am writing you this letter. I am writing it to praise you for your speech the other day in the National Assembly. Bravo, Kocho! Well, to tell you the truth, I was moved to tears of joy. I almost came over to you to give you a kiss in front of all the deputies. But they would have started stomping their feet, objecting... Do you remember which speech? How could you not? The whole world is talking about it. But you’re right, Kocho! For so many thousands of voters not to just tear apart twenty gendarmes and a drunken mob of fifty. Big deal! The gendarmes would have shot a hundred voters at most! Well, is that such a big deal? All in all, about two hundred households would have been left in mourning. Let’s say, next Sunday the army comes and they shoot, they kill at most, at most three hundred people. How many houses of orphans—five hundred houses! Quite a grand affair!...

And those fools, they actually started calming the crowd, making sure not a single hair was harmed! How can one not be outraged?... Thanks to such spineless fools, you waited a full eight years in Halki... To write them so many poems about stars and sighs, only for them to make you wait eight years. Eight years! A disgrace to the Bulgarian people. If at least a hundred thousand voters from all over Bulgaria had marched into the bullets, you could have taken your current cushy spot much sooner. What a worthless lot! Cowards! What the hell is the point of this legality and freedom if at least a thousand voters aren't slaughtered?... 

Keep it up, dear Kocho, that’s how I like you. Give such speeches more often to inspire greater confidence in the big shots... and then just enjoy yourself! So what if the younger generation resents it, so what if the people get agitated—don't you even blink an eye! The people! The people are a herd; once you start swinging the club... But then again, am I the one who has to teach you these things!...

I am most glad that it was you who rushed to give this speech; no one could beat you to it. Now then, if you haven't inspired confidence in them by now, when will you ever!... All the chorbadjis are praising you! "Bravo," they say, "Kocho has become one of us; he has finally come to his senses." Keep your wits about you now, stay on this path, and have no fear!... But always see to it, Kocho, that you set some money aside, for one never knows—the world is like a blossom!

Kocho, when you read this letter – tear it up, so it doesn’t fall into the hands of that fellow who described my travels through Europe, or he’ll splash me across the pages again somewhere. I heard him the other day, saying to someone: “My, what a pity, I didn't expect those words at all from our Velichkov”... and I listened to him and marveled at his wits. He’s full of hot air... Kocho, why are you still publishing that blasted “Progress”? Drop it! Truth be told, even its name is so childish; it no longer suits a solid man like you. And if you’re so itching to write – go ahead and write, but it would be most fitting to call the newspaper “It Is Not the Time” and then our partisans could be called “not-the-timers.”
I’ve brought a few vials in my saddlebags. Can’t you cook up some little law to have public buildings sprayed with rose oil?
